w10_P4_003322: A haulage yard keeps 376 chain links and 48 hooks, and both are issued in equal bundles of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That bundle size is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a tipper cage whose mass is 119000 g. The engineer works out the force the winch must apply to the cage to accelerate it that hard, then subtracts 28 N to allow for the counterweight. Because 7 identical cages hang from the same headframe, the headframe force is 7 times what is left. What force does the headframe carry, in kN?
w10_P4_003325: The figure the commissioning sheet ends on is 5 times a value that is 30 kJ more than the kilojoule reading described below. The total advance from the 0th to the 1st second, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a test slug whose mass is 28 kg. w10_P4_003326: Between the 2nd and the 3rd second of a stroke, a shuttle moves at a rate equal to 5 times the square of the elapsed time plus 2 times the elapsed time. The energy that mass carries because of its motion is recorded. The rail is 2.5 m long. What figure remains, in J?
w10_P4_003328: A store holds 270 bolts and 65 nuts, and both are drawn in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. w10_P4_003331: A launch controller adds its two dial settings 3 and 7, multiplies the sum by 5, and then subtracts 28 to fix the release speed, in metres per second, of a sled whose mass is 42000 g. w10_P4_003340: A workshop holds 43 drill bits and 137 collets, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. w10_P4_003343: A cam on a packaging machine gives the follower displacement as 2 times the cube of the crank angle plus 5 times the square of the crank angle. The force the drive must apply to the pusher to accelerate it that hard is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons. What load does the frame carry, in kN?
w10_P4_003358: During the first 2 seconds of a lift, a hoist drum pays out cable at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 3 times the elapsed time. w10_P4_003365: The number the log ends with is 8 times the kilojoule figure described below.
